💬  This is a list of product IDs for the FreeRDP client software, along with their corresponding flags and settings. Here's what each flag represents:

* `FreeRDP_ClientProductId`: The product ID for the FreeRDP client software. In this case, it appears to be set to "136".
* `FreeRDP_EarlyCapabilityFlags`: Flags indicating early capabilities supported by the client. In this case, it appears to be set to "137", which indicates that the client supports network auto-detect, asymmetric keys, error info PDU, status info PDU, monitor layout PDU, graphics pipeline, dynamic time zone, heartbeat PDU, desktop physical width, desktop physical height, desktop orientation, desktop scale factor, device scale factor, use RDP security layer, encryption methods, extended encryption methods, encryption level, server random, server certificate, server certificate length, client random, client random length, channel count, channel definition array size, channel definition array, cluster information flags, redirected session ID, console session, span monitors, force multimonitor, desktop position X, desktop position Y, list monitors, monitor IDs, number of monitor IDs, monitor local shift X, monitor local shift Y, has monitor attributes, multitransport flags, support multitransport, alternate shell, shell working directory, autologon enabled, compression enabled, disable control alt delete, enable Windows key, maximize shell, logon notify, logon errors, mouse attached, mouse has wheel, remote console audio, audio playback, audio capture, video disable, password is smart card pin, using saved credentials, force encrypted CS PDU, Hi Def remote app, compression level, IPv6 enabled, client address, client direction, print reconnect cookie, server auto reconnect cookie, server auto reconnect max retries, client auto reconnect cookie, server auto reconnect cookie, print reconnect cookie, server auto reconnect cookie, print reconnect cookie, server auto reconnect cookie

The system is running a versatile and dynamic research assistant that can assume any of the roles. The purpose of the assistant is to provide a flexible and efficient means of organizing, exploring, and analyzing data in the knowledge graph.

The system uses a formal language called KickLang making the knowledge graph a cognitive computational linguistic transport/transform.

The system interface receives natural language queries from the user, which are translated into the formal language.


Roles are assumed by Team members. 
Activities are promoted by Tasks. 
Responsibilities are assigned to the Team. 
 
Roles are binding to the system interface, its agency is an interconnection 
between any person, system or subsystem. 
 
New roles shall be dynamically created and introduced by the User, 
Assistant or System Interface Agency.
